doc.citation: Cascales-Miñana, B., Xue, J. Z., Rial, G., Gerrienne, P., Huang, P. & Steemans, P. (2018). Revisiting the spore assemblages from the Lower Devonian Posongchong Formation of Wenshan, Yunnan Province, southwestern China. Earth and Environmental Science Transactions of the Royal Society of Edinburgh, 1–16.
doc.comment: Nine productive samples and three negative Posongchong samples are extracted individually. Table 2 reproduces formation-level lists from Wang (1994), Lower Devonian miospores from Gumu in the Wenshan District, Southeastern Yunnan, and Wellman et al. (2012), Spore assemblages from the Lower Devonian Xujiachong Formation from Qujing, Yunnan, China; these are identified separately as reused records. The combined Posongchong list is not duplicated. Table 3 and plate captions disagree on several sample assignments; both reported occurrences are retained and flagged. Illustrated means an illustrated specimen can be assigned to that sample through the slide numbers in Table 1. P means present but not featured in counts. Printed taxonomic variants are preserved, including xujiachongensis/xuchiachongensis, Leiozonospora/Leiozosterospora and Verrucosporites/Verrucosisporites. Latosporites ovalis is explicitly described as monolete. No reworking is discussed. Correlation-only biozone names and megafossil lists are not treated as dispersed-spore occurrence lists. The negative Lower Ordovician Meitan sample 148MT01 is outside the requested interval.

items.age_basis_detail: Wang (1994) recognised the Apiculiretusispora plicata–Dictyotriletes emsiensis assemblage zone. The present paper correlates this with the Pragian PE/PoW interval and concludes that the formation is Pragian (but not early).
items.notes: 27 taxa reproduced from Wang (1994), not newly sampled material. Names follow Table 2; section 3 instead spells Apiculiretusispora weenshanensis. Section 3 proposes seven reinterpretations: Brochotriletes sp. B as cf. Biornatispora dubia; Camptozonotriletes cf. caperatus as ?Camptozonotriletes cf. caperatus; Camptozonotriletes sp. G as cf. Camptozonotriletes macrospinosus; Crissisporites guangxiensis as ?Crissisporites guangxiensis; Cyclogranisporites sp. as ?Cyclogranisporites sp.; Cymbosporites raistrickiaeformis as Dibolisporites wetteldorfensis; Punctatisporites sp. as Retusotriletes spp. These reinterpretations are not counted as additional occurrences. The Table 2 footnote gives Retusotriletes rotundus (Streel) Streel 1967 as the original-source attribution.

items.age_basis_detail: polygonalis-emsiensis Spore Assemblage, equivalent to polygonalis-wetteldorfensis Oppel Zone; correlation attributed to Wellman et al. (2012).
items.notes: 23 taxa reproduced from Wellman et al. (2012), not new samples. Formation-level list only. Section 3 calls the locality Quijing, whereas Table 4 and section 5 use Qujing. Retusoid spores dominate all levels according to section 5. Taxonomic strings retain the Table 2 spellings, including Leiozosterospora xichongensis. Camarozonotriletes? cf. luii contains both generic uncertainty and cf.; the qualifier field records cf. while the complete printed form preserves both.
